title: Parabolic Interpolation Peak Finder
description: Three adjustable bin magnitudes with a fitted parabola and a marker at the interpolated sub-bin peak position, with the formula worked out numerically.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Peak Detection
Numerical Methods
chapter_title: Windowing, Spectral Leakage, and Peak Detection

learningObjectives: Calculate the parabolic interpolation offset from three magnitudes
Demonstrate how the estimated peak shifts between bins
Verify the symmetric case gives zero offset
prerequisites: A spectrum is magnitude per bin

equations: parabola: y(t) = ((alpha+gamma)/2 - beta) t^2 + ((gamma-alpha)/2) t + beta
assumptions: The centre bin is the local maximum
The peak shape is approximately quadratic near its top, which holds for windowed data
limitations: Least accurate for a rectangular window, where the peak is not well approximated by a parabola; the denominator is guarded against the collinear case

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Formula plus geometric consequence, manipulated directly
keyQuestions: What offset do symmetric neighbours give, and why must that be so?
What check must precede this formula in real code?
commonMisconceptions: That the nearest bin is the best available frequency estimate
That better resolution always requires a larger N
assessmentOpportunities: Compute delta for a given triple and state the peak's direction
